title: Sales enablement unified playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s core positioning and messaging, battlecards for key competitors, a recommended pitch-deck outline for prospects, pricing guidance for common buying motions, two representative case studies with metrics, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the canonical sales enablement reference for commercial and solutions teams.

Audience: AEs, SEs, Solutions Engineers, Sales Engineers, Partnerships, and RevOps.

Summary of value proposition

- Core positioning: Redwood Inference is the developer-first inference platform that makes production-grade LLM serving predictable, cost-efficient, and reliable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Primary benefits to emphasize: predictable latency & throughput (SLOs), cost controls (batching/caching/quant profiles), deployment flexibility (hosted -> dedicated -> private), and first-class observability + rollouts.
- Key differentiator: unified runtime + operational tooling that lets customers move from experimentation to production without re-architecting inference.

Target personas & buying triggers

1) Startup AI / Product engineering lead
   - Trigger: rapid feature velocity, PLG adoption, needs fast time-to-value with cost controls.
   - Messaging: fast onboarding, hosted API, cost/latency transparency, model catalog and SDKs.
2) Platform / Infra team at mid-market / enterprise
   - Trigger: standardization across teams, predictable throughput, security/compliance.
   - Messaging: Dedicated capacity, SLO-backed performance, autoscaling policies, RBAC & audit logging.
3) Regulated / security-sensitive buyer (finance, healthcare, gov)
   - Trigger: data residency, encryption, air-gapped deployment.
   - Messaging: Private deployment, KMS/HSM integrations, audit trails, compliance evidence.

Core messaging pillars (elevator pitches)

- For Product Engineers: "Ship LLM features without rebuilding inference — predictable latency, clear cost levers, and dev-friendly SDKs."
- For Platform Teams: "Standardize inference across teams with SLA-backed Dedicated capacity and centralized observability."
- For Security/Compliance: "Deploy inference in your VPC or on-prem with audit logging and customer-managed keys."

Competitive brief (high-level)

Primary competitors considered by prospects: Managed LLM API providers (A, B), cloud managed endpoints (C), and self-hosted inference runtimes (D).

Quick battlecard (use in calls):

| Topic | Redwood strength | Common competitor reply | Suggested rebuttal / focus |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Time-to-value | Hosted API + examples, SDKs, quickstarts | "We have managed endpoints too" | Emphasize curated model catalog, performance profiles, and community-ready templates that reduce integration work. |
| Predictability & SLOs | Dedicated capacity with SLA, autoscale policies | Competitor managed offerings vary on SLOs | Highlight SLA-backed tiers and concrete latency percentiles from our benchmarks. |
| Cost controls | Smart batching, KV caching, quant profiles | Cloud endpoints charge per second or GPU-hour | Explain per-token economics, batching/caching levers, and Optimize toolkit recommendations. |
| Private deployments | VPC/on-prem options + KMS/HSM | Some rivals either only managed or only self-hosted | Position Redwood as a consistent product across modes; customers keep same API & rollouts. |
| Observability | Token-level cost/latency breakdowns, tracing, rollouts | Limited visibility in many offerings | Walk through console screenshots and per-route dashboards during demo. |

Competitive positioning notes:
- Against managed APIs: lead with performance transparency + unit economics; demo cost and latency dashboards.
- Against cloud provider endpoints: lead with developer experience (SDKs, curated models) + cross-region fallbacks and SKU flexibility.
- Against self-hosted runtimes: lead with operational burden reduction, prod-grade autoscaling, and security add-ons (Private with audit evidence).

Pitch deck: recommended slide flow (15-20 minutes single-AE version)

1. Title / one-liner (30s): Who we are and what we deliver.
2. Problem (60s): The gap between prototype LLM features and production inference (cost, latency, reliability).
3. Opportunity (60s): How applications scale with reliable inference; customer outcomes.
4. Product overview (90s): Hosted API, Dedicated, Private — quick feature highlights.
5. Architecture (60s): Runtime + smart routing + caching/ batching + deployment abstraction (diagram).
6. Performance & economics (90s): Benchmarks, per-token cost examples, SLO examples.
7. Security & compliance (60s): VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO mentions where applicable.
8. Customer examples (90s): Short case study bullets with numbers.
9. Pricing & packaging (60s): Typical options and guidance.
10. Rollout & next steps (30s): PoC plan, timeline, success criteria.
11. Appendix: technical deep-dive and FAQ.

Slide-level talking points & assets to include:
- Screenshots: Console per-route latency heatmap, token cost breakdown, rollout controls.
- Snippets: Quick API call for generation and embeddings, config sample for Dedicated autoscale.
- Benchmarks: 99th/95th latency percentiles on curated models (include model names in appendix).

Pricing guidance (recommended approach for AEs)

- Offer three packaging tiers as a starting point:
  1) Self-serve Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation and per-embedding units. Good for early-stage customers and POCs.
  2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly or annual commit with predictable throughput; include burst capacity add-on.
  3) Private (enterprise): platform license + deployment + bandwidth/ support add-ons.

- Common negotiation levers: committed spend, minimum term, burst capacity limits, white-glove onboarding fees, longer retention/observability windows.
- Pricing playbooks:
  - POC / SMB: emphasize low friction, free credits, short trial with usage caps.
  - Mid-market: propose 12-month reserved capacity with a 10-20% volume discount and 1-2 dedicated support seats.
  - Enterprise: structure as platform license + implementation + annual renewals; include SLAs and compliance packs as add-ons.

Case studies (two concise examples for pitch use)

1) Search & Relevance startup (abbreviated)
- Customer: QueryFast (hypothetical).
- Challenge: Prototype model caused high token costs and tail latency impacting UX.
- Redwood solution: Deployed Hosted API during dev, then migrated to Dedicated with prefix caching and batching.
- Outcome: 3x reduction in per-query token cost, 60% reduction in 95th pct latency, launch to 10k daily active users.
- Quote: "Redwood let us ship faster and keep costs predictable during scale." — Head of Engineering, QueryFast

2) Regulated enterprise (abbreviated)
- Customer: Acme Health (hypothetical).
- Challenge: Data residency and audit requirements for patient-facing assistant.
- Redwood solution: Private deployment in customer VPC, KMS integration, audit logging, and dedicated support for rollout.
- Outcome: Passed internal security review, production rollout in 6 weeks, zero PII exposure incidents to date.
- Quote: "The Private deployment made our security team comfortable to proceed." — Director, Product Security, Acme Health

Security FAQ for prospects (short, shareable)

Q: Where do you store customer data?
A: By default, hosted API data is processed in our controlled environment with retention policies configurable per account. For customers requiring data residency, Redwood offers Dedicated and Private deployments where data remains inside customer network boundaries or regions.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. Private deployments support KMS/HSM integrations and Dedicated customers can opt into customer-managed key options for encryption-at-rest where required.

Q: What audit and logging capabilities exist?
A: The Redwood Console provides per-request audit logs, role-based access control, and configurable retention windows. Private deployments can forward logs to customer SIEMs and Support can provide compliance evidence packages.

Q: How do you handle model updates and rollbacks?
A: Our rollout tooling supports canary and A/B deployment patterns, automatic fallback to pinned model versions, and metric-driven rollbacks. We recommend pairing rollout policies with canary traffic for safe upgrades.

Q: How is data used for model training?
A: Redwood does not use customer proprietary data to train or improve models unless explicitly contracted and opt-in is granted. For hosted customers concerned about this, Private deployments ensure data never leaves the customer environment.

Q: What certifications/compliance posture do you maintain?
A: Redwood maintains internal evidence for SOC/ISO readiness and can provide compliance packages for enterprise customers; exact artifacts depend on deployment mode and contractual terms.

Recommended sales play / PoC checklist (technical + commercial)

1) Discovery (AE/SE)
   - Confirm persona, scale expectations (RPS, seq length, concurrency), compliance requirements, and success metrics.
2) PoC design (SE)
   - Decide mode: Hosted quickstart vs Dedicated PoC vs Private pilot.
   - Define dataset (anonymized or synthetic), traffic profile, and evaluation prompts/metrics.
3) Implementation (Dev/SE)
   - Provide quickstart repo, API keys, example code, and dashboard access.
   - Configure KV/prefix caching and batching where appropriate.
4) Measure & iterate (AE/SE)
   - Share dashboards with customer, review latency/cost metrics, identify optimizations.
5) Commercial (AE/RevOps)
   - Propose packaging with recommended commit, support level, and timeline to production.

Objections & suggested responses

- "We can host this ourselves to save money." -> "Self-hosting removes vendor operational burden but shifts engineering/time cost to your team. Redwood reduces time-to-production, provides SLA-backed Dedicated capacity, and a single API across modes so you can start hosted and move to private without re-architecture."
- "How do we control costs at scale?" -> "We provide per-token cost visibility, Optimize tooling with batching/quant profiles, and reserved capacity options for predictable unit costs. We’ll run a TCO comparison as part of the PoC."
- "What if performance degrades with scale?" -> "Dedicated capacity and autoscale policies, plus smart routing and KV caching, are designed to preserve latency SLOs. We also provide runbooks and on-call support during ramp."
